chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a man forgets the tashahhud in the salat and remembers that he said only “Bismillah,” then his salat has been valid. But if he does not remember anything from the tashahhud, he repeats the salat.

The correct understanding of this report is that if he remembers that he said “Bismillah,” then his salat is complete, and he completes the two testimonies by way of qaḍāʾ, and he does not repeat the salat.

And if he remembers nothing at all, he repeats the salat if he had left it deliberately. There is nothing in the report stating whether this applies when he did not remember it after leaving it forgetfully or deliberately.
And if he had left it inadvertently and then remembered, then the qaḍāʾ of the tashahhud would be upon him, as we have explained.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: the testimony recited in the sitting of salat
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies to be completed by way of qaḍāʾ
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up a missed part after its proper place
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: the phrase remembered as having been uttered in place of the full tashahhud

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the tashahhud in salat?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of one who omits the tashahhud in salat. It distinguishes between forgetful omission and deliberate omission, indicating that if some minimal remembrance remains, the salat stands and the tashahhud is made up later, whereas deliberate abandonment necessitates repeating the salat.
